message.content:
**Allele frequency of rs7412 (APOE ε2 allele) in Europeans**

| Source | Frequency (T allele) |
|--------|----------------------|
| 1000 Genomes Project (EUR panel) | ~0.07–0.08 (≈ 7–8 %) |
| gnomAD v2.1.1 (non‑Finnish European subset) | ~0.07–0.09 (≈ 7–9 %) |

> **Interpretation**  
> The rs7412 SNP is one of two key variants that define the APOE ε2/ε3/ε4 haplotypes. In most European ancestry cohorts, the T allele (which corresponds to the ε2 allele) is present at roughly 7–8 % of chromosomes. This frequency can vary slightly between sub‑populations (e.g., Northern vs. Southern Europeans) but generally falls within this range.

> **Why it matters**  
> The ε2 allele (rs7412 T) is associated with a lower risk of late‑onset Alzheimer’s disease compared with the ε3 allele, whereas the ε4 allele (defined by rs429358) confers higher risk. Knowing the allele frequency helps in estimating population‑level risk and in designing studies that require power calculations for rare variants.

> **Caveats**  
> - The figures above refer to *allele* frequency, not genotype frequency.  
> - Frequencies may differ in isolated or admixed populations; always check the specific cohort you’re studying.  
> - The numbers are derived from large reference panels (1000 Genomes, gnomAD) and represent contemporary European samples; historical or ancient DNA studies might report different values.

If you need the exact allele count or genotype distribution for a particular dataset, let me know the dataset name (e.g., UK Biobank, 1000 Genomes EUR, gnomAD v3) and I can fetch the precise counts for you.
